builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: UniPipe: Unified Inference Serving and Fine-Tuning for Deadline-Constrained DNN Surrogate Workflows
summary: UniPipe replaces the common practice of either freezing a pretrained surrogate or running fine-tuning in a separate CUDA context alongside serving, by fusing training and inference samples into one forward pass with a selective backward pass and an offline batch-composition scheduler on a single GPU. The cost is implementation complexity: a custom scheduler exploiting the non-linear latency-versus-batch curve, workload repetitiveness assumptions, and engineering to fuse training and inference batches, with some training throughput traded for latency stability. It can fail when the input stream is not repetitive enough for offline scheduling, when the GPU's latency curve does not exhibit the assumed non-linearity, or when fine-tuning on live data causes drift or instability without validation safeguards.
rationale: The technique targets a single-GPU constraint the reader shares and offers concrete deadline and accuracy gains, but its benefits depend on repetitive high-rate streaming workloads with online fine-tuning, so it warrants a pilot only if that deployment pattern exists.
technique: Single-context fused inference serving and fine-tuning

claims.statement: UniPipe replaces the common practice of either freezing a pretrained surrogate or running fine-tuning in a separate CUDA context alongside serving, by fusing training and inference samples into one forward pass with a selective backward pass and an offline batch-composition scheduler on a single GPU. The cost is implementation complexity: a custom scheduler exploiting the non-linear latency-versus-batch curve, workload repetitiveness assumptions, and engineering to fuse training and inference batches, with some training throughput traded for latency stability. It can fail when the input stream is not repetitive enough for offline scheduling, when the GPU's latency curve does not exhibit the assumed non-linearity, or when fine-tuning on live data causes drift or instability without validation safeguards.

Reduces deadline-miss rate by 13%-22% over a multi-context baseline, lowers inference MSE by up to 50% and reconstruction MSE by up to 30%, and cuts latency spread from 106% to 57% of the mean at sensor rates up to 5000 patterns/sec.
